bib.title: SELF-INSTRUCT: Aligning Language Models with Self-Generated Instructions
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 61st Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; Tables 10 and 11 example tasks skimmed

question: Can a pretrained LM bootstrap its own instruction-tuning data from a small seed set, and does tuning on it improve instruction following?
hypothesis: A vanilla LM prompted with a few human seed tasks can generate diverse, usable instruction data, so tuning on it approaches human-annotated instruction tuning with almost no annotation.
contributions: a method for inducing instruction following with minimal human-labeled data
release of a 52K synthetic instruction dataset and a set of manually-written novel tasks

method.summary: Iterative bootstrapping: sample 8 tasks from a pool seeded with 175 human tasks, prompt GPT3 davinci to write new instructions, classify them, generate instances (input-first or output-first), filter by ROUGE-L<0.7 and heuristics, add to pool. Finetune the same GPT3 on the 52K result via the OpenAI finetuning API.

prompts.text:
Come up with a series of tasks:
Task 1:
{instruction for existing task 1}
...
Task 8:
{instruction for existing task 8}
Task 9:

Can the following task be regarded as a classification task with finite output labels?
Task:
Given my personality and the job, tell me if I would be suitable.
Is it classification?
Yes

Come up with examples for the following tasks.
Try to generate multiple examples when possible.
If the task doesn't require additional input, you can generate the output directly.

Given the classification task definition and the class labels, generate an input that corresponds to each of the class labels.
If the task doesn't require input, just generate the correct class label.

evidence.quote: every finetuning experiment is trained for two epochs to avoid overfitting the training tasks

results.claim: Tuning GPT3 on its own Self-Instruct data lifts zero-shot SuperNI ROUGE-L from 6.8 to 39.9 (+33.1), near InstructGPT001 at 40.8.
results.setup: SuperNI eval set, 119 tasks x 100 instances, zero-shot (definition only), greedy temp 0; GPT3 davinci 175B finetuned 2 epochs on 52K generated instructions

results.claim: InstructGPT001 scores 40.8 ROUGE-L on the same SuperNI unseen-task eval.
results.setup: Same as Table 3; text-davinci-001 only because newer engines may have seen SuperNI test

results.claim: GPT3 finetuned on T0 training data (50K instances) scores 37.9 ROUGE-L, below Self-Instruct's 39.9.
results.setup: Same SuperNI zero-shot setup; 50K sampled instances covering all instructions
results.table: Table 3, row GPT3 + T0 Training, column ROUGE-L

results.claim: Adding Self-Instruct data to SuperNI training raises GPT3 from 49.5 to 51.6 ROUGE-L.
results.setup: SuperNI zero-shot eval; GPT3 175B finetuned on 50K SuperNI instances vs plus Self-Instruct data
results.table: Table 3, row GPT3SELF-INST + SUPERNI Training (Ours), column ROUGE-L

results.claim: Vanilla GPT3 scores 6.8 ROUGE-L zero-shot on SuperNI (T5-LM 11B: 25.7).
On the 252 user-oriented instructions, GPT3SELF-INST is 5% behind InstructGPT001 if Rating-B counts as valid, and beats T0 and SuperNI-tuned GPT3 by a large margin.
results.setup: 252 expert-written novel instructions, 1 instance each; two author-evaluators, A-D scale; reported numbers from one evaluator (A+B counted as valid); models in random anonymized order
results.note: Quote is split across a line break in the text cache; the gap is read from the text, Fig 6 gives counts only.

results.claim: Of 200 sampled generated instances, 92% have a valid instruction, 79% appropriate input, 58% correct output, and 54% have all fields valid.
results.setup: 200 random instructions, 1 random instance each, labeled by one expert annotator who is an author
results.note: Same table: instruction valid 92%, input appropriate 79%, output correct 58%.
results.table: Table 2, row All fields are valid, column Yes %

results.claim: Pipeline yields 52,445 instructions (11,584 classification, 40,861 non-classification) and 82,439 instances after filtering.
Subsampled data scaling: human-eval A-rate improves with more data but plateaus after about 16K instructions; SuperNI gain plateaus at around hundreds of instructions.
results.setup: GPT3 finetuned on subsets, 252 user-oriented set, human eval

results.claim: Replacing outputs with InstructGPT003 outputs and finetuning GPT3 beats the original Self-Instruct data by 10% (percentage rated A).
results.setup: Same 252-instruction human eval; all instances' outputs regenerated by InstructGPT003 given instruction and input
results.quote: by 10%, which suggests big room for future work

results.claim: Human-eval inter-rater agreement between two evaluators on the 4-class scale is kappa 0.57 in the body, 0.58 in Appendix B.2; kappa 0.75 for acceptable (A/B) vs not.
results.setup: 252 instructions, two authors rated all independently
results.note: Body text (Sec 4.4) prints 0.57, Appendix B.2 prints 0.58. Spearman rho = 0.81.

limits: Inherits LM tail-phenomena limits; gains may skew toward frequent tasks (Limitations).
May work best only for large models; no study of model size.
Risk of amplifying biases; difficulty producing balanced labels.
Only 54% of sampled instances are fully valid; output is the noisiest field.

Human eval by two authors who wrote the instructions; one evaluator's ratings reported; only GPT3 davinci tested; no seeds or variance; finetuning details (optimizer, lr, batch) hidden behind the OpenAI API.
